items.stem: Why should a developer avoid placing a SOQL query inside a for loop that iterates over many records?

options.text: It can exceed the governor limit on the number of SOQL queries per transaction
options.rationale: Correct: Salesforce enforces a per-transaction SOQL limit; querying in a loop quickly exhausts it. Query once and use collections.

options.text: SOQL cannot be written inside Apex at all
options.rationale: SOQL is fully supported in Apex; the issue is querying inside loops.

options.text: Loops are not allowed in Apex
options.rationale: Loops are allowed; the problem is the query placement.

options.text: It improves performance and is recommended
options.rationale: It harms performance and risks limit exceptions.

items.explanation: Correct: Salesforce enforces a per-transaction SOQL limit; querying in a loop quickly exhausts it. Query once and use collections.

items.stem: Which relationship type should you use so that deleting a parent record automatically deletes its child records and the child inherits the parent's sharing?

options.rationale: Correct: master-detail cascades deletes and the detail inherits sharing/ownership from the master.
Lookup does not cascade delete by default and children keep their own sharing.
External lookups point to external objects, not for cascade-delete here.
Hierarchical relationships are a special self-lookup on the User object.

items.stem: Which TWO are true about Apex unit tests on the Salesforce platform?

options.text: Test methods do not commit data to the database
options.rationale: Correct: test data is rolled back after the test runs.

options.text: A minimum of 75% code coverage is required to deploy Apex to production
options.rationale: Correct: production deployment requires at least 75% org-wide Apex coverage.

options.text: Tests can see existing org data by default without (SeeAllData=true)
options.rationale: By default tests are isolated and cannot see org data unless SeeAllData=true is set.

options.text: Assertions are optional and coverage alone proves correctness
options.rationale: Coverage without assertions does not verify behaviour; assertions are essential.
Tests run in sandboxes and scratch orgs as well.

items.explanation: Correct: test data is rolled back after the test runs.
